row: | Zhang et al., [*Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Language Models*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.00923) (TMLR 2024) | Two-stage fine-tuning (rationale from text + ViT image features, then answer) took a 738M T5 to 90.45% on ScienceQA, against 75.17% for few-shot GPT-3.5 with CoT and 83.99% for GPT-4. In a 200M text-only model, writing the rationale before the answer cut accuracy from 81.63% to 69.32% because the rationales hallucinated image content; captions recovered only 0.8 points. Fine-tuned small models, not a prompting result | [2302.00923](sources/zhang-2023-multimodal-chain-thought-reasoning-language.pdf) | [03](notes/03-core-techniques.md#chain-of-thought) |

edits.old:
![Multimodal CoT: the rationale combines what the text says and what the image shows before the answer](../sources/images/zhang-multimodal-cot-fig1.png)
*Image Source: Zhang et al. (2023)*
edits.new:
![Multimodal CoT: the rationale combines what the text says and what the image shows before the answer](../sources/images/zhang-multimodal-cot-fig1.png)
*Image Source: Zhang et al. (2023)*

The two-stage split exists because a one-stage chain hurt the small model. **A 200M text-only T5 fine-tuned on ScienceQA scored 81.63% answering directly and 69.32% writing the rationale first**: in 56% of 50 sampled errors the rationale hallucinated what the image showed. Adding image captions gained 0.8 points; fusing ViT image features into the encoder took the two-stage model from 78.57% to 85.31% ([arXiv:2302.00923](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.00923) (Zhang et al., TMLR 2024)). The setup is fine-tuning, not prompting. Our extrapolation: when a chain has to reason about an image, give the reasoning step the image, not a caption of it.
edits.why: Paper is already described in the CoT variants bullet (method + 90.5% vs ~76%, both match Table 4: 90.45 / 75.17-76.47) but never cited by arXiv ID. Adds the citation plus the paper's central finding (Table 2: 81.63 -> 69.32; Table 3: captions 79.37 vs 78.57, vision 85.31; Fig. 3: 56% hallucination). 11-applications.md line 176 already points here for Multimodal CoT.

doubts: Verdict borderline sharpens/extends: method and headline are in the note; the hallucination/rationale-first finding is new. Frontmatter sources of 03-core-techniques.md needs https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.00923. Origin trace (methodology intents) returns only FLAN-T5 (Chung et al., JMLR 2024, in repo under generative-ai/05-RL) -- backbone, not the idea; the CoT origin (Wei et al. 2022) is already cited in the section. row: | Yuksekgonul et al., [*TextGrad: Automatic "Differentiation" via Text*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.07496) (Nature 2025) | Backpropagates LLM-written critiques through a pipeline as "textual gradients". Optimizing a system prompt for gpt-3.5-turbo with GPT-4o as the critic, on 36 training examples, lifted GSM8K from 72.9% to 81.1% with instructions alone, matching DSPy's 8-shot bootstrapped prompt. Its headline 51% to 55% on GPQA for GPT-4o is test-time refinement of each answer (3 rounds plus majority vote), not prompt optimization | [2406.07496](sources/yuksekgonul-2024-textgrad.pdf) | [08](notes/08-prompt-optimization.md#dspy-and-programmatic-optimization) |

edits.old: It took GPT-4o's zero-shot accuracy on GPQA from 51% to 55%
edits.new: Optimizing a system prompt for gpt-3.5-turbo, with GPT-4o writing the critiques on 36 training examples, lifted GSM8K from 72.9% to 81.1% with instructions alone, matching DSPy's 8-shot bootstrapped prompt; its headline GPQA gain for GPT-4o (51% to 55%) came from refining each answer at test time, not from a better prompt
edits.why: Misattribution: the passage presents TextGrad as revising prompts, then credits it with GPQA 51->55, but that result is 'solution optimization' (§3.2, Table 2: 3 test-time update iterations + majority voting over answers). The prompt-optimization result is §3.3, Table 3: gpt-3.5-turbo-0125 GSM8K 72.9 -> 81.1 (DSPy BFSR 8 demos also 81.1); batch 3 x 12 iterations = 36 examples.
